easy.def: Hard to believe.
examples: The story is unbelievable.
It was an unbelievable jump.
An unbelievable view.

more.def: So surprising or amazing that it is hard to believe.
examples: Her story was unbelievable.
We saw an unbelievable sunset.
The size of the pumpkin was unbelievable.

easy.def: The brother of your mom or dad.
examples: My uncle makes me laugh.
Uncle Joe lives far away.
I visit my uncle in summer.

more.def: The brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt.
examples: My uncle taught me how to fish at the lake.
Uncle Raj plays the drums in a band.
Both of my uncles came to my birthday party.

easy.def: Not feeling good or nice.
examples: These tight shoes are uncomfortable.
The itchy sweater is uncomfortable.
I feel uncomfortable in the hot car.

more.def: Not feeling relaxed or at ease, or causing that feeling.
examples: The hard bench was uncomfortable to sit on for long.
He felt uncomfortable speaking in front of the class.
There was an uncomfortable silence after the argument.

easy.def: Below something.
examples: The cat is under the bed.
Look under the table.
We dug under the fence.

more.def: Below or beneath something, or covered by it.
examples: The mouse hid under the old wooden porch.
We played under the shade of the tall oak tree.
A turtle can stay under the water for a long time.

easy.def: Under.
examples: My shoes are underneath the bed.
The ball is underneath the car.
I wear a shirt underneath my coat.

more.def: Below or under something, often covered by it.
examples: We found the key underneath the flowerpot.
A tunnel runs underneath the river.
She wore a sweater underneath her jacket.

easy.def: To know what something means.
examples: I understand the rules of the game.
I do not understand this word.
Do you understand the game?

more.def: To know the meaning of something or how it works.
examples: After the teacher drew a picture, I understood the math problem.
It is hard to understand him when he talks fast.
She understands how the engine works.

easy.def: Knowing what something means.
examples: I have an understanding of fractions.
Her understanding grew.
He has a good understanding of math.

more.def: The knowledge you have about how something works or what it means.
examples: She has a good understanding of how plants grow.
Reading more gave him a better understanding of the world.
We reached an understanding about the rules.

easy.def: Kind and able to see how others feel.
examples: The teacher was understanding.
She gave an understanding smile.
He was understanding when I was late.

more.def: Willing to understand other people's feelings and forgive them.
examples: My coach was understanding when I missed practice.
An understanding friend listens when you are sad.
She gave an understanding smile when I tripped.

easy.def: Clothes you wear under your other clothes.
examples: Put on clean underwear.
The underwear is in the drawer.
Dad folded the underwear.

more.def: Clothes that you wear next to your skin, under your other clothes.
examples: Mom put clean underwear in my drawer.
Pack socks and underwear for the trip.
He folded the underwear and put it away.

easy.def: Sadly.
examples: Unfortunately, it rained.
Unfortunately, I lost it.
Unfortunately, we are late.

more.def: It is sad that; used to talk about bad luck.
examples: Unfortunately, it rained on the day of the picnic.
Unfortunately, I lost my hat.
Unfortunately, the store was closed.

easy.def: Clothes worn by a group of people.
examples: The firefighter wears a uniform.
Our team has a uniform.
The soldier wore a uniform.

more.def: Clothing worn by members of a group, such as a team, school or army.
examples: The team wore blue uniforms.
The nurse put on her uniform.
Our school has a uniform.

easy.def: A group of people or places joined together.
examples: The states form a union.
The workers formed a union.
A union of friends.

more.def: A group of people, states or countries that join together for a shared purpose.
examples: The United States is a union of fifty states.
The teachers formed a union to work together.
The union of the two clubs made one big team.

easy.def: The only one like it.
examples: Each snowflake is unique.
Your voice is unique.
My hat is unique. I made it!

more.def: Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.
examples: Every person's fingerprints are unique.
The museum has a unique collection of old toys.
Each zebra has a unique pattern of stripes.

related.def: Being the only one of its kind.

easy.def: A fixed amount used for measuring.
examples: An inch is a unit.
A pound is a unit of weight.
A minute is a unit of time.

more.def: A fixed amount used to measure something, such as an inch, a gram or a minute.
examples: A foot is a unit of length.
An hour is a unit of time.
The meter is a unit used in many countries.

easy.def: One part of a larger whole.
examples: Our class has a unit on space.
The building has ten units.
We finished the math unit.

more.def: A single part of a larger whole, such as a section of a course or a home in a building.
examples: Our science unit is about volcanoes.
The building has twelve apartment units.
She passed the first unit of the course.

easy.def: Everything there is: the Earth, the sun, the stars, and all of space.
examples: There are many stars in the universe.
The universe is very, very big.
Our Earth is a small part of the universe.

more.def: Everything that exists, including all the stars, planets, and space.
examples: Scientists use telescopes to study faraway parts of the universe.
No one knows how big the universe really is.
There are billions of galaxies in the universe.

easy.def: A school you go to after high school.
examples: My cousin goes to a university.
The university has a big library.
She will study at the university.

more.def: A large school where adults study for degrees after high school.
examples: My aunt studied science at a university.
The university has many buildings and a big football field.
Scientists at the university study the stars.

easy.def: Except if.
examples: We will walk unless it rains.
Take a coat unless it is warm.
Do not open it unless I say so.

more.def: Except if something happens or is true.
examples: We will have the picnic unless it rains.
You cannot go outside unless you wear a coat.
I will wait here unless you need me inside.

easy.def: Up to the time that something happens.
examples: Wait until I come back.
Stay until it stops.
Play until dinner.

more.def: Up to the time when something happens.
examples: Stir the soup until it boils.
We played outside until it got dark.
Wait here until your name is called.

easy.def: Up to a certain time.
examples: I sleep until seven.
Wait until noon.
Stay until Friday.

more.def: Up to a certain time or point.
examples: The library is open until eight o'clock.
We have a spelling test, but not until Friday.
The paint takes until tomorrow to dry.

easy.def: Not what you see every day.
examples: A blue apple would be unusual.
He has an unusual pet. It is a snail.
It is unusual for the bus to be late.

more.def: Not common or ordinary; different from what you expect.
examples: It is unusual to see snow here in April.
The house has an unusual round door.
She has an unusual name that people remember.
